text: Real square root selects the nonnegative root for a nonnegative input and returns zero for a negative input. Thus √4=2 and √(−4)=0, rather than a complex value. The definition first replaces the input by its maximum with zero, then applies the inverse of squaring on nonnegative reals. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L111).

On nonnegative real numbers, square root is the inverse of squaring and preserves and reflects order. Its domain already excludes negative inputs, so no extra sign hypothesis is needed. Zero maps to zero, every nonnegative value has a unique root, and the construction always selects the nonnegative branch. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L45).

The real square-root function always has a nonnegative value, even when its input is negative. On nonnegative inputs this is the usual choice of square-root branch; on negative inputs Mathlib returns zero. Consequently this unconditional statement does not assert that every real number is a square. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L143).

The total real square-root function vanishes exactly on nonpositive inputs. Positive inputs have positive roots, while both zero and negative inputs return zero. The weak inequality is essential: the familiar statement that only zero has square root zero requires restricting the input to be nonnegative. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L267).

For a nonnegative real input, its square root is zero exactly when the input is zero. The sign hypothesis makes the ordinary equivalence valid at the boundary as well as for positive inputs. It cannot be omitted: Mathlib also assigns square root zero to every negative real number. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L265).

Taking the nonnegative square root of a real square returns the absolute value of the original number. No sign hypothesis is needed because x² is always nonnegative. For example, √((−3)²)=3, so replacing the absolute value by x would be wrong for negative x. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L188).

If x is nonnegative, taking the square root of x² recovers x. The nonnegativity assumption selects the correct root, including x=0. Without it the result would be |x|; for instance, the square root of (−3)² is 3 rather than −3. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L180).

For x≥0, squaring its real square root recovers x, including at zero. The sign assumption is necessary for this identity: when x<0, Mathlib’s square root is zero, whose square cannot equal x. Without the assumption, the squared root is instead max(x,0). Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L177).

If x≥0, the square root of xy equals √x times √y for every real y. A negative y causes both sides to vanish under Mathlib’s convention, so a second sign hypothesis is unnecessary. Some sign restriction remains essential: taking x=y=−1 would otherwise give 1=0. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L365).

The inequality √x≤y is equivalent to y≥0 together with x≤y². There is no sign restriction on x: negative inputs have root zero and automatically satisfy the squared bound. The condition y≥0 is indispensable, since a nonnegative square root cannot lie below a negative number. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L227).

When y>0, the strict inequality √x<y is equivalent to x<y², even for negative x. Strict positivity of y matters: with x=−1 and y=0 the squared comparison holds but the root comparison fails. Mathlib’s negative-input value zero therefore explains the stronger boundary hypothesis. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L234).

For x≥0, the inequality x<√y is equivalent to x²<y, without assuming y≥0. If y≤0, both sides are false because the square root is zero and x²≥0. The hypothesis on x is essential; negative lower bounds would not support the same squaring equivalence. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L394).

For nonnegative x and y, comparing x with √y is equivalent to comparing x² with y. Both sign hypotheses are relevant. In particular, allowing y<0 would fail at x=0: the root comparison would be true because √y=0, while 0≤y would be false. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L239).

The inequality √x≤x holds precisely when x=0 or x≥1. Between zero and one the square root is larger than x, while negative inputs fail because their root is zero. The result includes both boundary values and needs no separate nonnegativity hypothesis. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L305).

A real square root is strictly positive exactly when its input is strictly positive. This remains correct for all real inputs because zero and negative numbers both receive square root zero. It is a statement about the chosen nonnegative root, not about both roots of a quadratic equation. Compared with [Lebl Cor.4.4.3](https://www.jirka.org/ra/realanal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean#L285).

Module rank is the supremum of cardinalities of linearly independent subsets. For vector spaces it agrees with dimension, but for general modules it need not count generators, and the supremum need not be attained by an independent subset ([Lampert’s example](https://mathoverflow.net/a/263053)). Infinite cardinal values are retained here, unlike the natural-number-valued finrank. Compared with [Axler Def.2.35](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Basic.lean#L68).

A finite module means one generated by finitely many elements, not a module with finitely many underlying elements. For example, the integers form a finite module over themselves despite having infinitely many elements. The definition also covers semiring modules and permits the empty generating family for the zero module. Compared with [Stacks Tag0518](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0518) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Defs.lean#L121).

Over a scalar semiring with only one element, every module also has one element, and this definition of finrank returns 1. Here linear independence is vacuous, so the singleton subset {0} is independent. This is a deliberate general-module convention; ordinary vector-space dimension assumes nontrivial scalars. Compared with [Axler Def.2.35](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finrank.lean#L64).

If a module’s cardinal-valued rank is at most a natural number n, its natural-number-valued finrank is also at most n. The hypothesis already excludes infinite rank, so the convention assigning zero to infinite rank causes no ambiguity. No freeness, finite generating set, or field structure is assumed. Compared with [Axler Def.2.35](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finrank.lean#L78).

Integers are congruent modulo n when their remainders agree, equivalently when n divides their difference. Negative moduli give the same relation as their absolute values. Modulus zero is intentionally allowed and then congruence means equality; modulus one relates every pair. Thus the definition extends the usual nonzero-modulus convention. Compared with [Aspnes §8.4](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Int/ModEq.lean#L31).

This is R[xᵢⱼ,det(X)⁻¹]: localization inverts every power of the generic determinant, exactly the coordinate algebra in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). R is any commutative ring. Rank zero is included: the empty determinant is one, so no extra inverse generator is needed. No field or nontriviality assumption is hidden. Checks pass: [isUnit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L113), [counit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L294).
The generic determinant becomes invertible.
Identity evaluation sends that determinant to one.

This sends a polynomial in matrix entries to its class in the determinant localization, preserving R and multiplication. The scalar-tower construction supplies precisely the usual p↦p/1 map of [Stacks, localization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM). Subsequent formulas use its algebra-homomorphism property; they do not assume that an arbitrary localization map is injective. Checks pass: [coordinateRingMap_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L78), [comul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L163).
The map is the canonical localization algebra map.
The localization map intertwines the explicit comultiplications.

The matrix has entry xᵢⱼ/1 in R[xᵢⱼ,det(X)⁻¹], obtained by applying the localization map entrywise. This is the universal invertible matrix underlying [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Invertibility follows from its unit determinant, rather than being an extra chosen matrix or a hypothesis that the base ring is a field. Checks pass: [localizedGenericMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L90), [isUnit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L113).
Each entry is the localized polynomial generator.
Its determinant is a unit.

The determinant of the localized generic matrix is the image of the polynomial determinant. This follows because determinants are polynomial expressions in entries, so every ring homomorphism preserves them. It identifies the element inverted in the construction of [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W), without requiring injectivity of the localization map or a domain. Checks pass: [localizedGenericMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L90), [comul_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L277).
The entries are images under the same algebra map.
The resulting determinant has the multiplicative comultiplication formula.

The determinant is a unit because the coordinate ring was constructed by inverting precisely the generic determinant. Thus “unit” means an element with a multiplicative inverse over any commutative base ring, not merely a nonzero scalar. This is the invertibility condition in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), also meaningful over rings with zero divisors. Checks pass: [det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L105), [map_antipode_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L268).
The determinant equals the image of the element localized away from.
Inverse-matrix evaluation supplies the intended antipode action.

This algebra map sends xᵢⱼ to ∑ₖxᵢₖ⊗xₖⱼ, encoding ordinary matrix multiplication in that order, as in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). It extends to the determinant localization because the determinant maps to its tensor square, a unit. The tensor-factor maps are used as homomorphisms; no injective-embedding assumption is needed. Checks pass: [comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L220), [comul_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L277).
The matrix-product formula on every generator.
The determinant maps to its tensor square.

The counit evaluates matrix coordinates at the identity matrix: diagonal entries become one and other entries zero. This evaluation extends to the localization since the determinant evaluates to one, so its inverse does too. It is the identity-point homomorphism of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), with values in the original base ring R. Checks pass: [counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L230), [counit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L294).
Identity-matrix evaluation on generators.
The inverted determinant evaluates to one.

The antipode substitutes the inverse generic matrix for the coordinate variables, as in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Lean defines matrix inversion even for singular matrices, returning zero there; that convention is harmless here because localization proves the determinant is a unit. Its inverse determinant is again a unit, making the substitution extend uniquely. Checks pass: [antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L238), [antipode_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L300).
The antipode gives genuine inverse-matrix entries.
The determinant maps to its ring inverse.

Two R-algebra homomorphisms from this localization agree once they agree on the original polynomial ring. Values on inverse powers are then forced by preservation of multiplicative inverses, the uniqueness argument of [Stacks, localization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM). The target may be a noncommutative semiring; this conclusion concerns existing homomorphisms and needs no localization-map injectivity. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_algHom_ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L667), [comul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L163).
The bundled generatorwise extensionality theorem uses this localization uniqueness.
A constructed localization homomorphism has the required restriction.

This packages the explicit matrix-product comultiplication and identity-matrix counit into a bialgebra. Associativity of matrix multiplication gives coassociativity, and the identity matrix gives both counit laws, matching [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). It is a deliberately selected structure, rather than a global instance that might accidentally use a different coalgebra on the same underlying algebra. Checks pass: [comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L220), [counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L230).
The selected comultiplication uses matrix multiplication.
The selected counit uses the identity matrix.

This adds inverse-matrix evaluation to the selected bialgebra. The two antipode identities reduce on generators to X⁻¹X=I and XX⁻¹=I, using the unit determinant already proved. Thus it realizes the Hopf algebra of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51) over arbitrary commutative rings; the named structure does not silently select another global coalgebra instance. Checks pass: [hopfAlgebra_comul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L450), [hopfAlgebra_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L459), [hopfAlgebra_antipode](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L468).
The stored comultiplication is the explicit localized map.
The stored counit is identity evaluation.
The stored antipode is inverse-matrix evaluation.

This object stores R[xᵢⱼ,det(X)⁻¹] together with its explicitly chosen matrix Hopf structure, realizing [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). Bundling matters: the carrier alone does not determine a comultiplication. The exported formulas retain matrix multiplication, identity evaluation and inversion; “commutative” describes the coordinate ring, not the generally noncommutative group of invertible matrices. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L597), [coordinateHopfAlgebra_counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L613), [coordinateHopfAlgebra_antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L624).
The bundled coproduct has the matrix-product formula.
The bundled counit has the identity-entry formula.
The bundled antipode has the inverse-entry formula.

This is the identity R-algebra equivalence between the raw determinant localization and the carrier of its bundled Hopf algebra. It changes the packaging, not the elements or arithmetic. The transport equations separately identify the stored Hopf operations with those of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51); an algebra equivalence alone would not assert those coalgebra compatibilities. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L567), [coordinateHopfAlgebra_antipode_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L587).
Comultiplication is transported through this equivalence.
The antipode is transported through this equivalence.

This is the universal matrix read in the bundled coordinate algebra: its entries are the images of the same localized variables under the canonical algebra equivalence. Its interpretation agrees with [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). The determinant remains a unit, so the bundle introduces neither a different matrix nor an additional invertibility assumption. Checks pass: [genericMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L495), [isUnit_det_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L503).
Each bundled entry is the canonical image of the localized variable.
Bundling preserves the unit determinant.

The bundled generic matrix still has invertible determinant. The proof transports the raw determinant and its inverse through an algebra equivalence, which preserves units over any commutative base ring. This supplies the ring-theoretic invertibility needed in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51); nonzero determinant alone would be insufficient over a general ring. Checks pass: [genericMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L495), [genericMatrix_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L509).
The bundled matrix has the transported generic entries.
Its actual inverse is transported from the raw invertible matrix.

Taking the inverse generic matrix commutes with the canonical change from raw to bundled coordinates. Its transported inverse is a left inverse, hence the unique inverse of this matrix with unit determinant. This checks the inverse-entry interpretation in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51); Lean’s fallback value for singular matrices never enters the argument. For every bounded linear map T between real or complex Hilbert spaces, this gives T = U√(T* T). The canonical U extends the isometry √(T* T)x ↦ Tx and vanishes on ker T. Both spaces are complete; neither finite dimension nor closed range is assumed. The norm identity supplies the required extension bound. The modulus of the adjoint is `T` composed with the adjoint of its polar factor:
`|T†| = T U†`, equivalently `|T†| = U |T| U†`.
**Left polar decomposition:** `|T†| U = T`.
The modulus has the same pointwise norms as the operator: `‖|T| x‖ = ‖T x‖`.
The polar factor of the zero operator is zero.
The polar factor is a partial isometry.

The closure of the range of the modulus is the orthogonal complement of the kernel of the
operator. This is the initial space of the polar factor of `T`.
